name: Simple linear attention language models balance the recall-throughput tradeoff
problem: Efficient alternatives to attention (H3, Mamba, RWKV) hold a FIXED-SIZE recurrent state, and that small state is exactly why they fail at recall - grounding a generation in tokens seen earlier in context.
mechanism: BASED: a simple architecture that INTERLEAVES linear attention with sliding-window attention, combining a large effective attention window over the compressed recurrent state with a precise local window. The contribution is the identification and mapping of the RECALL-MEMORY TRADEOFF: window size and linear-attention feature dimension are knobs that dial the state size along a Pareto frontier, from full-attention quality at one end to attention-alternative state size at the other. Plus IO-aware algorithms so the linear path is not slower than an optimised attention implementation.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract), both with baselines: 24x higher throughput on language generation than FlashAttention-2 when generating 1024 tokens with 1.3B-parameter models; and +6.22 accuracy points over the strongest subquadratic models (Mamba) on real-world recall-intensive tasks at matched perplexity. Models trained up to 1.3B parameters. The FlashAttention-2 baseline makes this one of the better-anchored claims in the batch.

MERGED FIELD BY FIELD - nothing was silently dropped:
  mechanism: the retired record's text was materially fuller (975 chars vs 587) and is RETAINED here rather than discarded. Its text: Names and measures the tradeoff explicitly, then takes the pragmatic route: SLiM attention with a gated retainable feature map plus a sliding-window (local) attention stack, running several linear-attention layers and then a few sliding-window attention layers. Sliding-window attention is added back precisely because it is the cheap way to buy exact local recall while keeping the recurrent state small. State size is a tunable knob: varying the sliding-window width and the linear-attention feature dimension walks the Pareto frontier between state size and recall, from near-full-attention quality down to the small state of pure SSMs. The state is fixed-size and constant in sequence length, so the model still has no KV cache in the attention layers (the sliding-window part is bounded by the window, hence constant in total context). The paper also supplies IO-aware algorithms, which matters because linear attention is otherwise slower than optimized FlashAttention.
  speedup_reported: the two records carried DIFFERENT text for the same paper. This record's text is retained and the retired record's variant is quoted so the difference is visible: "IO-aware algorithms give 24x higher throughput than FlashAttention-2 when generating 1024 tokens with 1.3B-parameter models, on the authors' GPU hardware (A100-class). Also matches the strongest sub-quadratic models such as Mamba on perplexity and beats them by 6.22 accuracy points on recall-intensive real-world tasks. The 24x is against FlashAttention-2 at a specific generation length and is a kernel-algorithm comparison; it does not carry over to models of other sizes or to engine-integrated paths."
